observations: Every new crate behaviour first appears alone on solid ground: ? box, striped sandwich, stack, then mud stepping boxes.
Main course density 10/14/6; the 10-box wall is a third of the main count; the secret course (27) nearly equals the main course (30).
No 1UP boxes: every life is in a ? box at a risky or hidden place (over Nitros, ostrich ledge, above a turtle, in the bonus).
Crates double as traversal tools: mud stepping boxes, the stack's striped top, the secret arrow.
Enemies are placed as tools next to crates (turtle springboard, ostrich platforms).
Explosives are confined to the optional secret course, with the green switch at its exit.
Checkpoints: C1 where the secret rejoins, C2 directly before the wall, the secret C after its easy first third.
Count traps concentrate in the optional route: arrow box, timed ostrich ledges, ground trio passed underneath.
The blue gem turns the wall from 'break' into 'avoid'; a striped crate in its top row is the intended stepping stone and the court prevents bypassing.

geometryObservations: Lethality ramps one step per encounter: a hurdle that cannot fail (O-S1-a) → mud that only slows (G-S1-a) → a lethal hole beside the path with a box at its lip (G-S1-b) → a full-width pit after a practice runway (P-S1-b, G-S1-c) → a pit with an enemy on its landing (G-S1-d).

Main-course gaps are short and generous: about three lethal pits of ≈2–3 u, each with ≥4 u of run-up; every other "gap" (two mud swamps, three rat pits) turns failure into delay. The first level punishes with time, not lives.

Rat pits are enforced descents and enemy locks: ≈5–6 u walled squares too wide to jump, which the player must enter; the trampoline exit appears only when every mole is dead. Mole count rises 2 → 4 → 4 (G-S3-a, G-S3-b, G-S3-d).
Enemy patrol axes escalate: across the path, so it can be timed past (E-S1-a) → along the path, so it must be engaged (E-S1-b) → waiting on a landing, engaged while landing (E-S1-c).
The turtle is taught in four steps: alone after C1 (E-S2-a) → a pair for the chain stomp (E-S2-b) → a pair hidden behind a hurdle (E-S2-d) → a springboard under a floating box (E-S3-b).

Targets above jump height are reached only with living steps — the turtle's belly in S3 and the ostriches' backs in the secret (P-X-f). The height ceiling is enforced by placing targets just above the jump, not by walls.
Timed living steps (the ostriches duck when approached) teach "use it now" with a soft failure: missed boxes and a retry, never a death.

The optional side-scroll secret holds every coupled challenge — occupied landings (G-X-a), a flier on a runway (P-X-c), a perch over Nitro (G-X-b), an enemy ladder (J-X-c). The main course keeps its hazards uncoupled.
Platform length is set by the enemy on it: the vulture runways are ≈10+ u for reaction distance; the turtle landing ledges are ≈3 u, just long enough to land beside a crawling turtle.
Walled corridors remove side falls from the main course, and the ≈5–8 u lane leaves room to steer around enemies, which is why the early enemies are optional (F2 POINT1: no need to kill).
Perches appear exactly where precision is needed: the ?/? perch over the Nitro floor and the rock before the last mud box give a stable take-off for a one-shot jump.
The closed court makes the 2 × 5 wall unavoidable, and its 2 u height is just above a clean plain jump (D2), so the no-break goal needs the slide-jump or the striped foothold (O-S2-b).
Checkpoints sit on wide enclosed floors (plaza, court) or on the secret's first safe ledge after its opening hops — never on a narrow ledge, a mud crossing or inside a pit.
geometryTransfer: Opening debut strip: a walled corridor 6–8 m wide (`wall` / `coastwall` sides), a 0.6–1.0 m `platform` hurdle across it as the first jump, then a soft strip (`groundSpeedLimit`, 3–4 m) beside the first multi-hit sandwich, an edge `pit` beside — not across — the path with a crate at its lip, and only then a full-width `pit` 2.3–3.5 m long after ≥10 m of runway (the running full jump covers ≈5.6 m, so the first gap is forgiving by design).

Enforced-descent trap pit: a sunken square 6–7 m across whose walls stand more than 7 m above the pit floor (beyond the ≈7.0 m double-jump ledge-grab reach) or end in an overhanging lip, two `grunt`s inside (four in the repeat) and a `trampoline` in a corner as the only exit. It never kills; clearing the enemies is the practical requirement for using the trampoline.

Living step to a height target: a `turtle` patrolling ±1–1.5 m directly under a crate whose underside is above ≈5.5 m (beyond double-jump head reach). Valid only if this engine's stomp bounce off a `turtle` plus the double jump reaches it — measure that bounce before authoring; Part IX gives crate and arrow bounces only.

Side-scroll secret with occupied landings (`zone` dir E): 3–4 m ledges with 2–3 m gaps (well inside the 5.6 m jump), each landing patrolled by a `turtle` with range 1–1.5 m so the jump is timed to its phase; then a ≥12 m runway with a `floater` swooping from its far end (≈1.3 s of warning at 9 m/s), a checkpoint after the first three hops, and a `mover` lift (axis y) as the one-way exit.

No-break vault gate: Crash's 2-high wall (2.30 m) is below our 2.85 m full jump, so use a 3-high wall (3.46 m, needs the double jump) spanning a closed 5–6 m court right after a checkpoint, with one multi-hit crate in its top row as the stepping stone.

Perch over a hazard: a 3 × 2 m floating `platform` 4.6 m (4 crates) above a floor of Nitro, reached by a ≈3 m jump, holding the life crates; a ledge 2.3 m lower and 3 m on carries the arrow that lifts the player to the next tier.
